page: Amazon Web Services m9gd.12xlarge is a general-purpose instance powered by the AWS Nitro hypervisor and custom AWS Graviton ARMv9 Neoverse-V3 processors. It features 48 dedicated physical cores running at 2.8 GHz with a single thread per core. The memory configuration provides 192.0 GB of RAM, translating to 4.0 GB per core. Local storage is bundled with a 2850 GB NVMe SSD instance store volume, and the network interface delivers a baseline bandwidth of 25 Gbps.

Benchmark data indicates strong multi-core performance, with stress-ng multi-core and PassMark CPU scores placing in the top 25%. Memory performance is highly efficient, achieving top-tier status in the PassMark memory score and strong read-only memory bandwidth. The instance excels in data compression and decompression, with single-threaded gzip and both single- and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression ranking in the top 10%. Database operations are highly optimized, as evidenced by top-tier results in PassMark database operations and Redis SET operations, which reached 136.39 million operations per second. Static web serving throughput also ranks in the top 10%.

While the ARMv9 architecture delivers high resource density and excellent qualitative cost efficiency for parallelized workloads, certain performance tradeoffs exist. For instance, LLM inference prompt processing for a small 135M model is top-tier, but text generation for the same model falls into the bottom 10%. Additionally, the Neoverse-V3 processor lacks x86-specific instruction sets such as AVX, AVX-512, and AMX.

This hardware profile is highly suited for high-throughput database hosting, memory-cached key-value stores, static web serving, data compression pipelines, and general-purpose containerized applications requiring fast local NVMe storage.
